headings.title: SMTO-SKL-0043 — This Drive file is too large to download

html:
SMTO-SKL-0043 — This Drive file is too large to download

GUID: 36213ccd-b9b5-5c64-aa88-e4d9fba1ae37
Slug: google-drive-download-too-large
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • The file is bigger than SMTO or Google allows for this kind of download, so SMTO stopped and didn't keep a partial copy. Google limits saved copies of Docs, Sheets and Slides to about 10 MB.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. For a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides, ask SMTO to export it in a lighter format, such as plain text or CSV instead of PDF. Google won't export these files above about 10 MB, and some formats are much smaller than others.
  2. If the file is very large, split it in Google Drive (for example, copy part of a sheet into a new file) and download the smaller pieces. Each piece can then fit within the size limits.
  3. If you often need large files, ask the person who manages SMTO to raise SMTO's maximum saved file size. SMTO caps the size of files it saves, and only an administrator can change that cap.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the saved file in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, including roughly how large the file is in Google Drive.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Drive transfer exceeded a size limit: Google reported exportSizeLimitExceeded, or the declared or streamed bytes exceeded min(artifact max_file_bytes, 256 MiB download / 10 MiB export), or the artifact store hit its size quota.

What this means

  • Google reports exportSizeLimitExceeded, or declared/streamed bytes exceed the effective Drive transfer or artifact-file size limit. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google reports exportSizeLimitExceeded, or declared/streamed bytes exceed the effective Drive transfer or artifact-file size limit.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare provider export limits, declared size, streamed bytes and artifact quota.

How to fix it

  • files.save caps transfers at min(ArtifactLimits.max_file_bytes, 256 MiB) for downloads and min(max_file_bytes, 10 MiB) for exports; Google also returns 403 exportSizeLimitExceeded, and ArtifactStore artifact_size_limit maps here. Use a smaller file or export format; for downloads, raise AOR_ARTIFACT_MAX_FILE_BYTES / AOR_ARTIFACT_MAX_RUN_BYTES (defaults 64 MiB and 512 MiB) within the 256 MiB hard cap. The 10 MiB export cap cannot be raised.
  • Use a smaller file or export; exports are limited by Google to 10 MB and artifacts obey configured quotas.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use a smaller file or export; exports are limited by Google to 10 MB and artifacts obey configured quotas.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported smaller transfer fits all applicable bounds.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
